title: Hoovering
description: Attempts by a toxic individual to suck a victim back into a relationship after a breakup or period of no contact.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Named after the vacuum cleaner, hoovering is the mechanism used to suck a target back into the cycle of abuse after an escape. When a manipulator senses they are losing their supply (because the victim left, or went no-contact), they will deploy highly calibrated tactics—ranging from extreme apologies to manufactured crises—to force re-engagement.

sections.title: Manipulator's Objective
content: Re-establish control and dominance.
Extract emotional supply (even negative attention is supply).
Prevent the victim from moving on successfully.
Satisfy their ego by proving they can still 'win' the victim back.

sections.title: How The Tactic Works
content: Step 1: The relationship ends or the victim establishes hard boundaries.
Step 2: The manipulator waits for the ideal moment of vulnerability (holidays, anniversaries, or times of stress).
Step 3: The manipulator creates a highly tailored message designed to trigger empathy, guilt, or nostalgia.
Step 4: The victim responds. The door is cracked open, and the cycle of Idealize/Devalue begins again.

sections.title: Common Tactics Used
content: The Manufactured Crisis: 'I'm in the hospital / Someone died. I didn't know who else to call.'
The Pseudo-Apology: 'I finally went to therapy and realize you were right about everything.'
The Nostalgia Bait: Sending a picture of an old memory or song. 'Thinking of you.'
The Accidental Text: Sending something meant for 'someone else' to force you to ask about it.

sections.title: Real Conversation Examples
content: Manipulator (6 months post-breakup): 'I know you probably hate me. But I just drove past our old coffee shop and broke down. I miss my best friend. Please just tell me you are okay.'
Victim (feeling empathetic): 'I'm okay. Hope you are well.'
Result: The Hoover succeeded. Communication is re-established.

sections.title: Escalation Pattern
content: Early stage: Random likes on social media, casual 'checking in' texts.
Middle stage: Long emails declaring total transformation, sending unwanted extravagant gifts.
Advanced stage: Showing up at your workplace, threatening self-harm if you don't answer, or using friends/family as flying monkeys to relay messages.

sections.title: Why Victims Fall For It
content: The Hope for Closure: Victims want to believe the abuser finally 'gets it'.
Trauma Bonds: The brain is physically addicted to the manipulator and experiences the message as a dopamine hit.
Guilt: The crisis hoover is specifically designed to make you feel like a monster if you ignore them.

sections.title: Early Warning Signs
content: They only contact you when they see you are doing well without them.
The messages ignore the massive boundaries you previously set.
They attempt to jump right back into the 'idealization' phase, skipping past the reasons you left.

sections.title: Advanced Warning Signs
content: They create fake social media accounts to bypass your blocks.
They contact your mother, sister, or best friend with 'concerns about your well-being'.
Constant push-pull cycles where you break up and get back together multiple times a year.

sections.title: Protection Strategies
content: Absolute No Contact. Block numbers, block all social platforms, block emails.
Understand that the 'new them' is a mask. The mask will drop within weeks of you returning.
Log the bad times. Keep a list of exactly why you left, and read it when a hoover attempt happens.

sections.title: Counter-Moves
content: Fails: Replying with anger. 'Don't ever contact me again you psycho.' (This teaches them they still control your emotions).
Works: The Black Hole. Total, utter, agonizing silence. Messages go unread and unanswered.
Works: If a crisis is claimed: Call a neutral third party (their family) to handle it, do not handle it yourself.

sections.title: Reality Check
sections.content: Sometimes people do genuinely miss you and reach out. However, a healthy person respects boundaries. A hoovering manipulator views your boundaries as a game to win and will bulldoze them.
